title: What is the area of this rectangle?
description: A rectangle has sides of five point seven centimetres and thirteen point three centimetres. Both sides are written as tenths and multiplied as fractions to give hundredths. Keeko doubts that the area is sixty five point two one square centimetres.
teaching_notes: One idea: the area of a rectangle is one side multiplied by the other, and two decimals multiply as two fractions over ten. Watch for students who multiply the whole parts and the decimal parts separately and join them.

source: Find the area of the given rectangle: 5.7 cm by 13.3 cm
video_script.why: The child has multiplied a decimal by a counting number and now multiplies two decimals, as in finding an area.
video_script.substitution: the book's rectangle, five point seven centimetres by thirteen point three centimetres
video_script.anchor: A rectangle with sides of five point seven centimetres and thirteen point three centimetres, as in the book
video_script.wrong_answer: sixty five point two one square centimetres
video_script.wrong_move: A common slip multiplies five by thirteen to get sixty five and zero point seven by zero point three to get zero point two one, and joins them as sixty five point two one. Two mixed parts are left out, and the area is far below the size check of about seventy eight.

final_answer.spoken: seventy five point eight one square centimetres

maths_rules: area of a rectangle = side × side = 5.7 × 13.3
the slip: 5 × 13 = 65 and 0.7 × 0.3 = 0.21 give 65.21, with 5 × 0.3 and 0.7 × 13 missing
video_script.design: One idea: an area is one side multiplied by the other, and tenths times tenths make hundredths. Assumes the multiplication of decimals as fractions. Wrong idea: joining the whole parts product and the decimal parts product. The rectangle stays all video; the area appears only on the answer beat.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The area of a rectangle counts the squares of one centimetre that cover it.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>A rectangle with four rows of three squares has twelve squares.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>We get the same number by multiplying one side by the other side.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, one side is five point seven centimetres.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The other side is thirteen point three centimetres.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, the area of a rectangle is one side multiplied by the other side.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>We have to multiply five point seven by thirteen point three.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, write each side as a fraction with ten at the bottom. Five point seven is fifty seven over ten.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Thirteen point three is one hundred and thirty three over ten.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The area is these two fractions multiplied together.

marks.m1: the rule multiply the tops and multiply the bottoms is written
marks.m2: the tops and the bottoms are multiplied
marks.m3: the fraction seven thousand five hundred and eighty one over one hundred is written

beats.colours: the tops and the bottoms in two colours
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, multiply the tops and multiply the bottoms.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>On top, fifty seven times one hundred and thirty three. At the bottom, ten times ten.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>That gives seven thousand five hundred and eighty one over one hundred.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 7581/100 = 75.81; the area is 75.81 sq cm

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The area is now known.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Seven thousand five hundred and eighty one hundredths is seventy five point eight one.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The area is seventy five point eight one square centimetres.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks the area is sixty five point two one square centimetres.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Keeko multiplied only the whole parts and the decimal parts. The two mixed parts are missing from the rectangle.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>A size check helps. Six times thirteen is seventy eight, so the area must be near seventy eight.
